notes.title: DevBlog #03
notes.content:
[h1][b]MoonLight - CommunityManager[/b][/h1]

Hello there Maians! Today, we finally have a few updates about the state of Yomaia that we think it might interest you.

As a starting point, we want to share a sincere and detailed update regarding the development of Yomaia, an incredibly challenging project that continues to move forward with unwavering determination. Over the past few months, we’ve experienced a rollercoaster of emotions, obstacles, and lessons learned. 

We want to be fully transparent with you about what has happened and the decisions we’ve made along the way.

[h2]Challenges and Setbacks:[/h2]
The development of Yomaia has been [i]a unique experience[/i], but [u]also extremely difficult[/u]. During this time, we faced moments of frustration due to internal issues with some of our developers. These team members failed to meet their responsibilities, missed deadlines, and, most concerningly, diverted resources from the project. This situation forced us to take legal action, which has delayed our progress more than we initially anticipated. However, we are pleased to inform you that we won the legal disputes, which has allowed us to move forward with the project, although at a slower pace than we would have liked.

[i]This period of difficulties also required us to replace the employees who were dismissed due to their poor practices.[/i] The search for new talent has taken longer than expected, as [b]we are determined not to repeat the same mistakes.[/b] To this day, [i]we are still in that process[/i], which continues to affect the development speed, but we are committed to doing things right.

[h2]A Shift in Project Direction:[/h2]
After much reflection from the team, we have concluded that, due to limitations in resources and personnel,[u] we cannot continue developing the game as an MMO at this time[/u]. Yomaia was originally planned as a massive multiplayer online (MMO) game, but [b]we have decided to take a different approach[/b], at least temporarily.

To ensure a solid and high-quality product, we have decided to shift the direction of Yomaia and [b]focus on developing it as a Single Player experience[/b]. This decision will allow us to improve as developers and also provide us with the opportunity to [i]refine the gameplay and narrative in a more manageable and controlled environment.[/i] Once we have the single-player mode fully polished, we will be able to [b]repurpose many of those resources[/b] for the future MMO mode, which will enable us to deliver a more robust and seamless experience across both worlds.

We want to make it clear that [u]Yomaia will still be an MMO in the future[/u], but we need more time to perfect this aspect of the game and provide the best possible experience. For now, we will focus on delivering a complete and immersive experience, starting with the Single Player mode.

[h2]Updates and Details on the New Map:[/h2]
We are pleased to announce that the map for the Single Player mode, [b]Zone A[/b], is [b]nearly complete[/b], and we will soon be sharing videos showcasing how it looks. We have invested a significant amount of time and resources into this new phase, utilizing advanced tools such as Fluid Flux to ensure the highest quality in visual experience and environmental design. We want every corner of the map to immerse you in the world of Yomaia, and we have spared no expense in making it as realistic as possible.

[h3]The Single Player Mode:[/h3]
Regarding the Single Player mode, [i]it will be based on classic first-person Survival Horror[/i], from the perspective of a human trapped in a hostile and terrifying world. This mode will seamlessly blend gameplay with narrative, taking suspense and tension to extreme levels. We are committed to reviving the legendary beginnings of Survival Horror, where every decision and movement counts, and where the story intertwines with gameplay to create an unforgettable experience.


We would like to sincerely thank all of you, our incredible community, for your patience, support, and understanding. We know that delays are never easy to accept, but we want you to trust that this is the best decision to ensure Yomaia reaches the market in its best possible version. The coming months will be crucial, and with your support, we are confident the game will reach the level of quality we all expect.

Please stay tuned for future updates, where we will share more details about the game, and feel free to join us on Discord for the latest news.

[b]Once again, thank you for your continued support.[/b] Yomaia is still moving forward, and while it may take a little more time, we promise it will be worth the wait!

Sincerely,
[b]The Yomaia Development Team[/b]

notes.title: DevBlog #02
notes.content:
[h1]Time Lord - Full Stack Developer[/h1]
Greetings and welcome to another Yomaia Dev Blog our dear Maians. Here, I'll provide insights into the ongoing development progress of the game over the last months. I am sure you all will find in this new blog entry an awesome experience!

[h3]LOCOMOTION[/h3]
Over the past months, I've dedicated my efforts to [i]refining the locomotion mechanics[/i] for four iconic dinosaurs: T-Rex, Utah, Dilo, and Para. While Rex, Utah, and Dilo presented relatively smooth progress, Para introduced some unique challenges. Para boasts the ability to transition between bipedal and quadrupedal locomotion with the simple press of a button, introducing intriguing variables such as speed, turn speed, and run speed. [u]Triceratops is also being worked on[/u]. We're also implementing multiple movement mechanics including walk, trot, run, and sprint, each governed by a stamina bar that replenishes over time. Additionally, we're incorporating features like jumping, swimming, and even flying for select creatures. Progress is steadily propelling us towards completion.

[previewyoutube=nQFuwHf2-dU;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]TEST MAP[/h3]
A single, compact map will serve as a comprehensive[i] testing ground for each creature[/i], featuring various testing elements such as healing and damaging plates, a waterfall to assess footstep effects, slopes to evaluate climbing mechanics, and more. The map will encompass diverse terrains including grasslands, forests, oceanic regions, and pools for aquatic testing.

[h3]UI[/h3]
Development is underway for the in-game UI/HUD, which will include a [b]dynamic blood screen[/b] to visually represent health status – intensifying as health decreases and diminishing as it rises. Additional attribute indicators will dynamically display various statistics, with [b]a unique heartbeat monitor[/b] serving as an innovative health gauge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/444c9d486add2c6e69d70634a1c1bc4e48f27f53.png[/img]
[h3]CHARACTER MECHANICS[/h3]
We've revamped the health mechanic and are currently refining the [b]feeding system to replenish health[/b], incorporating mechanics for drinking water and maintaining hydration. Furthermore, we're enhancing damage mechanics to encompass various forms of injury.

[h3]GAME MECHANICS[/h3]
Our focus is on structuring the game's progression sequence and delineating areas for player exploration. 

[h3]OPTIMIZATION[/h3]
Efforts are underway to [b]optimize assets and code to ensure smooth gameplay performance across target platforms.[/b] Despite the incorporation of dynamic weather systems, we aim to provide a seamless gaming experience for our players.

[h1]Alicia - 3D Modeler and Lead Animator[/h1]

If I were to meticulously recount the amount of tedious work I've had to undertake in these past months, I wouldn't finish, so I'll try to brief.

Don't be mistaken, the result, as you can see, is tremendous! Texture mapping has gone from scale to scale almost satisfying as point-to-point animation. I've delved into [b]the latest scientific discoveries to strive for the best quality and realism in both appearance and movement for each creature[/b], adding specific [u]touches requested by the Project Leader[/u] for each dinosaur. However, as I mentioned, all of this has been an incredibly headache-inducing endeavor. Yet, I can't deny that I would do it all over again a thousand times to deliver this kind of quality that we're achieving now.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/0884f7a0e396c24c691a0245366429fcfc5a42b8.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/655bc3ffee5f2153824d1beacb807b652974d057.png[/img]
During this time, I've meticulously focused on improving textures, UV mapping, animations, and assembling them in Unreal alongside Time Lord, also focusing on the proposed roster for the[b] Early Access launch with 10 dinosaurs[/b] (5 from the hunter faction and 5 from the herbivore faction). This has allowed us to almost complete the initial roster and several more for the future that only need a touch-up, focusing our resources on delivering fewer models, but of higher quality, rather than many that feel like walking stones.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/72c5ea772b99e5423a0dab63b53db9a6a98d136b.png[/img]
However, certain aspects with the animations have been a challenge for me more than once, as it seems that Unreal Engine 5 has some love-hate relationship with locomotion, although it's already been resolved. It's safe to say that, as of today, we're perfectly oriented on this matter and everything is on track regarding the development of the remaining animations. I'm excited about all of this, I won't deny it. It's gratifying to see how the animals one creates take shape and come to life, knowing that someone will choose one of your dinos as their favorite! I can't wait for you to see the wonderful animations I've achieved after having to recycle, more than once, dozens of them because I refused to deliver that quality of work. I love this game, and I'll give my best so that you can enjoy a true game where dinosaurs feel alive and organic.

[previewyoutube=vw_paF1mZiU;full][/previewyoutube]
[h1]Mario - UI/UIX Editor[/h1]

I can proudly say that all UI/UIX-related content has been perfected and is already [b]being applied to the game system[/b] with Knever. I've strived to maintain the essence dictated by Central regarding the appearance and feeling on the interfaces. Our UIs aim at [i]blending elements of 80s-90s aesthetics with futuristic elements[/i], resulting in a visual spectacle that I consider magnificent. I've given a personal vintage touch to the iconic artistic style of four decades ago, while also incorporating futuristic elements harmoniously into certain interfaces. As a reference point, I could describe this work in interface design, for example, as the almost perfect union (though I say this humbly) between the style from the 80`s Alien film and Prometheus. This may seem trivial, but Central was very specific about [b]wanting User Interfaces that were intuitive and easy to navigate and reflected the game's lore[/b], having an appearance and quality that would impress the player upon seeing them. We want the player to be stunned not only by how intuitive it is when they access the game but also by how visually organic it feels for the gameplay style. And that's exactly what we've achieved! I'm completely confident that more than one will dedicate themselves to exploring the interfaces more than actually playing the game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/a93e7361dd2c756dbc5f9c2d5d9d14e9369b60b0.jpg[/img]
I bet that more than one person will feel incredible nostalgia as soon as they see the interfaces throughout the game and how they function. Including the sound!

[h1]Knever - Lead Programmer[/h1]

I'm thrilled about Yomaia;[b] this game offers an array of unique features.[/b] Joining the team recently, I've spent the past two months refining and integrating the work already completed by my teammates. With every passing day, I grow more confident in the tremendous potential of this game. As you see down below, I just needed to play a bit of the game with another developer, and all was settled for me. I'm eager to contribute my creative ideas to this project, aiming to see it through from inception to release, ensuring it's accessible to our entire player base. While our efforts are diverse, your support remains crucial.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/0663ac56eb9b844fb860674a5ef53a6bcac7472f.jpg[/img]
As a programmer, I can attest that Yomaia boasts a plethora of UI elements to convey vital information. I've taken the helm in this area, implementing my ideas while aligning with Central's vision to craft an exceptional experience for all players. Some UI elements have been finalized, while others remain a work in progress. I'm excited to reveal that our themes will incorporate darker tones with subtle nods to scientific inspiration. Upon launching the game, players will be greeted by a welcoming screen, guiding them seamlessly through server selection, character class/type selection, and dinosaur selection. Additionally, players can expect a skin selection feature offering a variety of choices, alongside a character stats panel providing insight into their current status and statistics.

Furthermore, I've dedicated significant effort to refining the locomotion system, a challenging task but one that aligns with Central's vision. Rest assured, we're making significant progress, and you'll soon witness the results firsthand! Stay tuned for more updates!

[h1]CentralCovenant - Project Leader[/h1]

Although I want to refrain from extensive commentary in our Dev Blogs, preferring to reserve this space for technical development content or the insights and perspectives of each developer, numerous inquiries across our social media channels have prompted me to offer a brief update on the game's development from my role as PL, as well as outline our plans for future blog and marketing announcements.

Firstly, I want to address the fact that I mentioned months ago that there would be another blog entry detailing the progress of Yomaia. Honestly, I can't recall if I notified anyone on Discord about the delay of said entry. Nevertheless, I apologize for the delay and my silence in failing to explain why there haven't been any updates on Steam or other non-Discord platforms about the game's development for such an extended period. Don`t worry, everything is proceeding smoothly. We are certainly not a developer team who abandons a project midway. On that note, everything is progressing well, despite encountering some unforeseen delays.

Regarding the aforementioned, I would like to officially specify my idea and plan concerning Dev Blogs and their publication frequency. I understand that many of you are used to other games that release monthly blogs, but frankly,[b] I believe that is the biggest mistake a developer can make.[/b] Let's be realistic, not everyone takes the time to read every detail in these blogs or pays attention to what's being said, resulting in an illogical diversion of community resources and a monotonous stream of words that players won't appreciate or value if it's constantly bombarding them every month. This is the reality, and I understand it. Therefore, [u]I've decided that our Dev Blog updates will occur every few months, providing more extensive and comprehensive updates on the game's development.[/u] This will make our blog entries something that people genuinely anticipate from us, rather than a tiresome monthly message cycle that ultimately becomes burdensome for both you and us. As the saying goes: Good things come to those who wait. Or in this context: Less is more.

We are not (and I am foremost among them) like others who make promises and then fail to deliver, or fill pages with thousands of entries that ultimately say nothing. I am honest with you: [i]I prefer to show you five completed models than to inundate you with a bunch of technical jargon about minor adjustments.[/i] Less talk and more action, that's how I want to operate. Therefore, from now on, please understand that if you don't see monthly Dev Blogs, it's because I have intentionally decided against it. Every few months, you'll receive a substantial update on our Steam page or social media channels, rather than one every month or week. This way, we avoid overwhelming both ourselves and you.

On another note, we'll begin to [b]increase our activity on social media[/b], as we're approaching our internal deadline for the Early Access release. It's time to start moving, and that's precisely what we'll do. I caution you, though, it will be a gradual and organic process. We have some interviews and announcements lined up for the near future that I'm confident you'll enjoy. Yomaia has been quieter over these past few months, following a strategic plan, but that's about to change. So, to all those who have inquired or had doubts about why we've been so quiet, you now have your answer. I also recommend that all of you join [url=https://discord.gg/S5h9cdQDPM]our Discord[/url], which is and will always be the place with the most constant flow of updates and news.

With that said, I believe my part here is done. It's a pleasure to provide you with new information about the plans and ideas we have for the development, and I hope to see you all increasingly excited about this game, which will undoubtedly captivate more than a few unsuspecting souls!

Until next time, Maians! Watch your back!

notes.title: Dev Blog #01
notes.content:
[h2][b]Alicia - 3D Modeler and Lead Animator[/b][/h2]
Hello everyone, this month has been quite a roller coaster for many of us, filled with a lot of effort and determination to deliver an unparalleled product. Central pulled one of its usual surprises this month, causing me to shift my focus from completing the juvenile and sub-adult models of our already finished models to concentrating on creating and finalizing all the models for our main roster. As a result, I am now entirely dedicated to crafting the remaining dinosaurs in their adult versions. After that, I plan to enhance our existing models that were already completed, such as the Tyrannosaurus or Triceratops, making them more accurate and of higher quality, as you can see below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/6de2dfa968fb9f51287aaf7809fe7ce1c97a4c04.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/84458824762ec3a184c09c348a260bc3c618bfcd.png[/img]

In a short while, we will have all 20 main roster dinosaurs for the Early Access fully completed and ready for animation, awaiting inclusion in the Technical Demo to showcase what we are capable of.

[h2][b]Time Lord - Full Stack Developer[/b][/h2]
In August I completed a significant portion of the current in-game map (Zone C) in accordance with the Project Leader's requirements. The Project Leader is the one who specifies every detail of how each area of the map should look, as he has a very clear vision of how things should appear and how to convey the desired atmosphere to players exploring the area. The entire coastline and a substantial part of the interior of the map have been finished, pending the addition of laboratories, buildings, and some significant natural landmarks.

I also focused on the swampy area and the main rivers of the map, getting ready to start modeling the cave system, underground rivers, and the untouched northeastern area.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/dfb5c2a9ba044c5103020612c9644d174bfe8e35.png[/img]

Additionally, I worked on AI implementation, Night Vision, HP system implementation, a Blood Screen for when the player takes damage, a Health UI widget to monitor remaining health, a Footprint function for the dinosaurs, a loading screen required for transitioning to another game level, and finally, the addition of a new playable character: the Ankylosaurus.

The AI was initially developed through the CHARACTER blueprint but is now undergoing modifications to function through a behavior tree, resulting in a more natural appearance and behavior.
Night vision and HP implementation were achieved similarly, with the use of post-process materials from the character blueprint.

The Blood Screen effect is accomplished through a user interface material on a widget, where opacity is directly proportional to health. The lower the health, the more prominent the blood on the screen, and it even blinks. Furthermore, the Health UI is connected to the health implementation on a widget to provide real-time health monitoring.

Footprints are created using notifiers, materials, and the CharacterBP, applied to a plane to display the material.

Regarding the loading screen, I encountered some challenges due to Unreal Engine's limitations in handling video. Nevertheless, with some patience, I was able to overcome these issues.

[h2][b]Mario - UI/UIX Editor[/b][/h2]
This month, my focus has been on completing all the essential HUD elements for players, including stamina, hunger, thirst, and various status changes. I've also finished all the necessary components for the species selection menu and the character selection menu. 

After thorough testing of these elements, I can officially announce that we are ready to implement these menus and user interfaces in the game, allowing players to choose their desired dinosaur and species when entering the game server.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/f0aee120371e2ebe3a8cd3216effdc435fa72e1e.png[/img]

[h2][b]JoeTheLycan - Video Editor[/b][/h2]
To be honest, it's been a fun but challenging month. I recently completed the loading screen that will appear during transitions. However, what could have been done in two weeks was extended to five, thanks to Central's idea of incorporating hidden messages in the loading screens and all audiovisual elements. This decision was made because the game's lore and storytelling will involve these methods and many more unconventional ones.

I recommend examining all these elements closely; you may discover more than a few secrets if you scrutinize what I'm doing carefully!

notes.title: DevBlog #00
notes.content:
[h1][b]Central Covenant - Project Leader[/b][/h1]

Hello everyone! Welcome to the first Yomaia Dev Blog, where you can delve deeper into our game. As many of you already know, I'm Central Covenant, and in this inaugural Dev Blog, I, as the boss, game owner, and Project Leader, reserve the right to use it as an "introduction letter" to explain and present what Yomaia is all about. I aim to provide clarity to our followers on our development progress, our intended approach, and what you can expect from the different phases of our game.

As you are aware, Yomaia is a Survival Horror MMO, a massively multiplayer game that immerses players in an intense survival experience, allowing them to embody both carnivorous and herbivorous beasts and beings, as well as humans. It showcases the immense potential of each species and presents a challenge to determine the ultimate champion.

In the Survival aspect, whether playing as dinosaurs or humans, the game revolves around the struggle to survive on an expansive map (island), where conditions, including weather and gameplay mechanics are perpetually against the player. Survival is at the core of the game, encompassing tasks such as feeding, drinking, managing stamina, adapting to diverse temperatures based on different map sections, and even delving into the intricacies of reproduction and forming groups. These elements collectively contribute to the Survival Horror experience that defines Yomaia.

Throughout the game, players will encounter various challenges, such as navigating the darkness of night, where instincts and unique abilities as a dinosaur or human will be essential for survival. Additionally, the map features specific areas like laboratories that can be accessed by dinosaurs of suitable size. However, it is important to note that there are far more dangerous entities than mere dinosaurs lurking within these locations. Even if you are the largest creature around, there will always be a more formidable threat hidden in the depths of the map, capable of unleashing chaos upon the land at any given moment.

At Yomaia, we aim to create a truly immersive and thrilling experience, where players must navigate a hostile environment and confront their deepest fears. We have carefully crafted an intricate world where danger lurks at every turn, ensuring that each playthrough is filled with suspense, adrenaline, and unexpected encounters.

[h3][b]ROSTER[/b][/h3]
Regarding our dinosaur roster, our initial plan for [i]Early Access[/i] is to launch a [u]group of ten carnivores and ten herbivores[/u]. However, we may start with fewer species initially and gradually expand the roster based on feedback. From a sustainable development perspective, [i]we propose starting with five carnivores and five herbivores as minimun[/i], which may change and improve over time. We will use player feedback to add the remaining dinosaurs in a more refined manner.

[b]INTENDED EARLY ACCESS ROSTER[/b]

[list]
[u]CARNIVORES[/u]
[*] Tyrannosaurus Rex, Spinosaurus, Giganotosaurus
[*] Ceratosaurus, Carnotaurus, Allosaurus, Suchomimus, Baryonix
[*] Deinonichus, Dilophosaurus

[u]HERBIVORES[/u]
[*] Triceratops, Stegosaurus, Ankylosaurus, Therizinosaurus
[*] Iguanodon, Parasaurolophus, Corythosaurus
[*] Pachycephalosaurus, Gallimimus, Dryosaurus
[/list]

[b]This will be our complete roster for the Early Access[/b] version. However, please note that we are referring specifically to the Early Access version, which will undergo updates and improvements. While we strive to add more species at the start of Early Access, we are still in the process of finalizing and preparing them. We have plans to include a significant number of additional dinosaurs, and we are open to community suggestions for additional species. As we transition from Early Access (alpha playable) to the beta phase, our aim is to introduce AI-controlled dinosaurs first, followed by playable ones.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/668f48efe157a7fa9e37764d39711dc3afe74255.jpg[/img]

We greatly appreciate and encourage community proposals, and we will make efforts to implement them as quickly as possible. In terms of gameplay, Yomaia offers [b]high replayability as each dinosaur has its own unique playstyle, mechanics, and skills[/b]. Additionally, each [i]species will have its own exclusive skill tree[/i], known as the [b]DNA evolutionary chain[/b], providing players with different ways to play and develop their dinosaurs. Although this may not be immediately apparent at the beginning, it is a feature we plan to fully implement.

For example, each dinosaur's skill tree will allow players to choose between [u]three different types of mutagens[/u], which significantly impact the gameplay experience. By selecting different mutagens, players can modify the way they play with a particular dinosaur. This dynamic gameplay system offers various possibilities. For instance, taking mutagen A in the first line, mutagen B in the second line, and mutagen C in the third line will create a different experience than taking mutagen B first, followed by mutagen C and then mutagen A in subsequent games. This dynamic approach ensures that each encounter with a dinosaur feels unique, as their abilities and gameplay mechanics change based on the chosen mutagens.

Furthermore, [b]every dinosaur will possess its own set of special mechanics[/b]. For example, the Kentrosaurus, a smaller species resembling the Stegosaurus, has spikes on its tail and back. When the Kentrosaurus attacks with its tail, it inflicts bleeding damage on the target. Additionally, the dinosaur has a passive ability that enhances bleeding damage inflicted when another dinosaur bites it from behind or from the sides, depending on the location of the spikes. This example illustrates how each dinosaur will have species-specific mechanics, such as bone-breaking, localized bone damage, and armor, which give them advantages in certain situations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/d5b8e66a3b61624f3b37eb8537f1a1f28327165f.png[/img]

However, in Yomaia, we will also feature [i]human characters divided into two factions:[/i] the [b]Biogenesis Corporation Military Branch[/b] and the [b]Test Subject branch[/b].

[b]The Biogenesis Corporation Military Branch[/b] offers unique roles, including the [b]trapper, engineer, Shock troop, support, and healer[/b]. [i]Only five players can play as military characters per server[/i], and each role provides exclusive gameplay. For example, the trapper specializes in temporarily immobilizing dinosaurs or using tracking darts to locate them. The healer focuses on supporting and healing teammates, even having the ability to revive them. The Shock troop serves as a tank with high damage and resistance, capable of engaging and eliminating dinosaurs if necessary. The engineer is responsible for activating traps, unlocking areas, and solving puzzles to assist the team in achieving objectives. The Biogenesis Corporation Military Branch not only engages in survival but [i]also has missions across the map to unlock resources and reach the core of the island.[/i] By reconstructing the hidden artificial intelligence of the Biogenesis Corporation, they gain powerful buffs that make them capable of facing dinosaurs with less difficulty.

To balance gameplay, we will limit the number of players in the military faction to five per server. [i]If all five roles are already filled, new players will enter a waiting queue[/i]. If a player occupying a role leaves, the next player in the queue will fill that vacancy. This approach ensures a balanced team composition.

[u]In the event that a player dies, the next player in the queue automatically takes their place.[/u] This mechanic allows for continuous gameplay and leveling of the team. The military group has access to various tools and vehicles such as choppers, jeeps, and more if necessary. By limiting the number of players per server to five, the game is kept balanced and fair.

[u]The humans are the only group with the ability to craft[/u], with the military faction having a lower crafting capacity compared to the next group, the [b]Test Subjects[/b]. The [b]Test Subjects represent the survival-focused and crafting-oriented branch of humans.[/b] Players will start as male or female characters within three human subspecies: [b]Caucasoid, Negroid and Mongoloid[/b] , each with unique attributes. Starting with minimal resources, [i]players must focus on survival, collecting resources, and crafting items[/i]. This aspect of the game will resemble survival-focused games like ARK.

Both the military and the test subjects will have access to the abandoned laboratories and industrial areas within the Biogenesis Corporation labs. However, the military faction will have access to more specific areas compared to the test subjects. Nonetheless, test subjects will also have unique areas to explore due to their crafting abilities.

While dinosaurs may have limited access to these areas, they will depend on humans to unlock or open them through specific actions or passages. [i]Only smaller dinosaurs will be able to access these areas directly, while larger dinosaurs will need to wait for certain events or conditions to occur[/i] before entering the laboratories.

In conclusion, humans in Yomaia will possess unique abilities and gameplay mechanics, just like the dinosaurs. Within the human factions, the Biogenesis Corporation Military Branch and the Test Subject branch offer distinct gameplay experiences. The development team plans to introduce also a robust [b]underwater ecosystem and underwater caverns[/b] in the future, allowing for [i]underwater gameplay when aquatic dinosaurs are added[/i]. The goal is to create a seamless experience where players can choose to play as a dinosaur or a human, and within those choices, engage in gameplay on land, in the air, or underwater. The addition of underwater lab sections and a well-developed underwater ecosystem ensures that players who prefer underwater gameplay won't feel left out. 

[i]Please note that while these features may not be fully implemented during Early Access, they are part of our plans for the beta version.[/i]

So, from the development team, our primary focus is to provide the community with diverse and immersive gameplay within our game. Players will have the opportunity to experience the game in various ways, including exploring the underwater habitat. It's important to note that the underwater habitat will be part of the same map, not a separate map. However we also have plans to implement fully dedicated underwater maps, allowing players to choose whether they want to play exclusively in the sea, on land, or both, especially when setting up their own servers.

Speaking of servers, our intention is to establish [b]centralized servers in each major region[/b]. Initially, there will likely be one server per region. [i]Our servers will have the capacity to accommodate between three hundred and five hundred players[/i], although meeting these requirements may take time as we are a growing development team. However, we will strive to achieve this goal, and it's possible that we may even reach it by the beginning of the Early Access phase. We appreciate your understanding and support during the development process.

At the outset, the gameplay we offer will be foundational, though enjoyable and with a considerable amount of content. However, it's important to note that the amount of content available will significantly expand over time, [i]potentially within six months or more[/i].

Returning to the topic of servers, our plan is to have [b]centralized servers in North America, South America, Europe, and Australia[/b], with a minimum capacity of three hundred simultaneous players. If demand exceeds the capacity of these servers, we [u]will consider opening additional servers based on the community's needs and feedback[/u]. While I have the final say as the game's creator, I value and listen to the community's input. If, for example, the North American server consistently reaches its capacity and players request more server space, we will gladly accommodate their needs. However, for [i]regions like China or the Middle East, we will need to assess the game's capacity and the population's interest[/i] to determine whether it warrants additional server support.

[h3][b]MECHANICS[/b][/h3]
The game will feature a robust set of mechanics that aim to make Yomaia the best survival horror game ever, with a focus on incorporating special, general, and unique elements that set it apart from other games in the genre. One notable example is the [b]map mechanics[/b]. What does this mean? [u]The map itself will be interactive, requiring players to adapt their gameplay in certain areas[/u] due to specific mechanics that can either complicate or favor their approach. In these areas, you will notice variations in temperature, with [i]some regions being colder or hotter[/i]. As a human or dinosaur player, you must exercise caution, as entering an area unsuitable for your species [b]can result in debuffs such as hypothermia or heatstroke.[/b]

Additionally, the map will have [u]zones that only specific dinosaurs can access[/u]. This design choice aims to activate the survival element within the community and groups, as well as encourage gameplay diversity across different dinosaur species. [i]The intention is to avoid a scenario where players exclusively favor one dinosaur, such as Rex, and neglect playing other species.[/i] However, it's important to note that [b]accessing certain areas of the map may require waiting for specific events, changing to a different dinosaur, or accepting that certain areas will remain inaccessible.[/b]
Another aspect of map mechanics includes [b]environmental events[/b] such as [b]droughts[/b], [b]landslides[/b], and [b]hurricanes[/b], which can be considered as atmospheric processes. These events will directly impact the map, affecting gameplay dynamics. For instance, [u]lakes can fill up and flood during certain seasons, while rivers may overflow or dry up[/u]. These changes will both enhance and hinder different types of players, who must adapt their strategies accordingly. Hurricanes, for example, may pose a threat to smaller dinosaurs, requiring them to seek shelter in caves or other designated areas. The survival challenges presented by these events extend to larger dinosaurs as well. Droughts can lead to limited water sources, resulting in intense competition for survival, especially considering that some dinosaurs require more water than others. [b]These map mechanics and environmental events[/b], including droughts, floods, hurricanes, and even snowfall that can decrease the temperature below freezing, [b]create a dynamic and unpredictable gameplay experience[/b].

These  mechanics represent a unique feature in Yomaia that, to the best of our knowledge, hasn't been implemented in any other game to date. Or at least, not with this relevance. They contribute to making Yomaia a truly immersive and authentic survival game. Moreover, besides the environmental and map mechanics, we also incorporate specific mechanics tailored to individual dinosaur species. For example, the Kentrosaurus and Ankylosaurus possess [b]distinctive abilities[/b]. The Ankylosaurus, with its tail club, can deliver devastating blows, while its thick armor greatly reduces the damage it receives. When facing an Ankylosaurus, players will need to adopt specific strategies to overcome its defensive capabilities. Furthermore, we plan to implement a [b]localized damage system[/b] that will add depth and strategy to melee combat, allowing players to utilize various techniques to overcome barriers.

These dinosaur-specific mechanics, as well as the mechanics applicable to humans, ensure that Yomaia's combat system goes beyond simple hit-and-run or repetitive strategies. The combat system aims to be ambitious, offering localized damage, dynamic combat mechanics, and enjoyable, intuitive gameplay that requires thoughtful decision-making. This applies not only to combat but also extends to other aspects of the game, such as test subjects and crafting.

In addition to these mechanics, we are focusing on intrinsic game mechanics that will be integral to Yomaia's main mode: Survival. [i]We aim to achieve a realistic or semi-realistic style without relying on external rules since not all players may have access to our Discord or other communication channels[/i]. These intrinsic [b]game mechanics will guide players to adopt a semi-realistic playstyle without imposing excessive restrictions or unrealistic rules.[/b] While players will still have the freedom to play as they wish, it's important to note that [u]certain actions may result in buffs or debuffs that can significantly impact their gameplay experience[/u]. For example, we have implemented a [b]population control mechanic[/b] to [u]prevent issues like overpacking or mixpacking[/u], depending on the class and species of the dinosaur. 

The visual representation of these population control mechanics appears as a red (or green for buffs) icon in the corner of the user interface, accompanied by a name such as "stressed predator." Players can find more information by accessing the dinosaur's user interface and selecting the corresponding icon. Depending on the dinosaur type and the acquired debuff, players may experience a damage reduction of 35 percent or more. Despite the potential debuffs or penalties, we do not intend to prohibit any particular playstyle, as it would be counterproductive. However, these game mechanics will naturally encourage players to engage in a semi-realistic or realistic playstyle, minimizing issues like overpacking or mixpacking.

Overall, these mechanics, encompassing map interactions, dinosaur-specific abilities, and intrinsic game mechanics for reproduction, combat, survival, feeding, hunting, scavenging, air, weather, etc, aim to make Yomaia a standout survival game, offering a comprehensive and immersive gameplay experience. [b]We will explain the mechanics in detail in a future Dev Blog[/b] where all the mechanics are described. 

[h3][b]RAIDS[/b][/h3]
One exclusive type of event in Yomaia is the Raid. Raids are [u]special areas[/u] such as caves or dungeons [u]that can be unlocked by certain actions performed by players on the map[/u]. Once unlocked, certain groups of [u]dinosaurs or humans can access these areas to face a mutant boss[/u]. As a dinosaur, [b]defeating the boss can grant genetic buff that allow for mutations and growth in specific ways, leading to improved gameplay. As a human, engaging in Raids can provide better loot.[/b] However, these benefits are lost upon death.

[b]The Raid system is still under discussion[/b], but it is an exciting feature that we believe the community will enjoy. Players will face mutant bosses, such as a combination of Triceratops, Velociraptor, and a human, and by defeating them and consuming their meat, players will receive unique rewards and access evolutionary advancements for their dinosaurs.

[h3][b]ALPHAS[/b][/h3]
Moving on to another point, we are proud to introduce the Alpha system. [b]These mechanics serve as an End Game feature[/b], [i]allowing players to enter in the challenge mode once they reach their maximum adult potential[/i]. By accessing the Alpha System through the skill tree and consuming other players to unlock certain skills, players can unleash their Alpha version. [b]The Alpha version represents a more powerful and beastly form of the dinosaur compared to the regular models[/b] seen from small to adult stages. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/35ecb0e385bedc49ce5f95ff88dc773cc92b4d1c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/3778fa5bc9e1072b2e2a937afd825c33637e8b87.jpg[/img]

Because[b] every species within Yomaia will have the ability to become the Alpha of their species[/b] within the server, it will not only change their way of playing and their abilities, but also their overall experience. For instance, if we have an Alpha Spinosaurus, becoming an Alpha will transform their gameplay. However, to become an Alpha, certain post-game requirements must be fulfilled. Once the dinosaur reaches its fully grown stage, it needs to meet specific criteria and compete with other players to claim the Alpha position. Once someone becomes an Alpha, they must maintain their title.
What does being an Alpha mean? It means that the [b]server can only accommodate two Alphas[/b]. As soon as a third Alpha emerges, or even with two Alphas, [i]an icon will automatically appear above each of them, allowing Alphas to locate one another.[/i] This system is designed to make the Alpha title [u]a reward for those who excel or possess superior gameplay skills.[/u] However, it also limits the raw power of the Alpha and encourages rotation within this role. In other words, anyone can achieve Alpha status, but once you reach that stage, you'll be directed to eliminate the other Alpha at the risk of losing your own dinosaur.

These mechanics will be further explained in the mechanics section or through our Discord server for any clarifications. We are extremely proud of this system in Yomaia, as it is a unique endgame or post-game mechanic that sets us apart from other games. It ensures that players won't get bored of their gameplay experience and enjoy of a big variety of choices.

[h3][b]DEVELOPMENT & IDEAS[/b][/h3]
In this stage of development process, we are currently dedicating a significant amount of effort to finalize the animation process for all possible models. We are animating both the basic models and the alpha models, which is an enormous task and requires double the effort. Rest assured that we are striving to release the game in Early Access as complete and polished as possible.

I'd like to explain also our ideas regarding [i]Skins and our concept surrounding them[/i]. As a developer, my intention is to give the game a visual aesthetic with realistic dinosaurs. However, as always, we want to offer the option for players to choose a more stylized dinosaur appearance that they may be familiar with from various sources. Therefore, we have implemented the concept of [b]Skin Models[/b] and [b]Basic Skins[/b] in the development process.

The [b]Skin Models[/b] concept corresponds to a [u]skin that completely changes the appearance of the model and potentially even certain animations.[/u] On the other hand, we have [b]Basic Skins[/b], which [u]only alter color patterns and similar aspects[/u]. Players will have the freedom to choose from various types of skins for each dinosaur, whether male or female, within the options we provide.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/976c7a7ef1d4d0e474e87a3ddb952b2d7b2c2d00.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/563059abc783f746bbe0528f3f94a512988f6e3a.png[/img]

Thanks to this type of skin development, we can virtually implement infinite possibilities that allow players to customize their dinosaurs not only in terms of color and pattern, but also in terms of model. This feature is one of the main attractions of Yomaia. Players will have a [b]wide selection of specific options for both male and female[/b] dinosaurs, including [b]special skins that can change the model and appearance of their dinosaurs.[/b] It's important [i]not to confuse this color and skin selection mechanic with the previously mentioned Alpha models[/i], which closely resemble the Jurassic Park style. [b]Skin models are only applicable to the basic models[/b], namely [b]juvenile[/b], [b]sub-adult[/b], and [b]adult[/b]. The Alpha class has only one type of model, with variations in skin depending on the gender.

As the level desing development, our intention is to create at least [b]three different maps[/b] on each server, namely [b]Zone A[/b], [b]Zone B[/b], and [b]Zone C[/b]. Each map will consist of various sections and interactive areas, as explained earlier, featuring themes such as flooding and drought. We take it a step further by implementing interactive areas within the maps that can be unlocked from one side to another. For example, reaching a base at one end of the map as a human player may require coordination with a teammate at the other end. By simultaneously pressing a switch in a specific area, players can unlock a main area of the Biogenesis Corporation laboratories. This development process brings unprecedented dynamism to the game, enhancing both player experience and exploration within the map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43573855/93abbaf5f01e46557201c35191ede61bc256c6b2.jpg[/img]

With this level of map desing, players can work as a team within their respective areas, [i]unlocking secrets and discovering interactive zones[/i], thus expanding the gameplay within the map. Additionally, our intention is to create [b]distinct biomes within the maps[/b]. For instance, [i]Zone C features a heavily forested and tropical landscape[/i], resembling a rainforest island with plains and swamps. On the other hand, [b]Zone A is predominantly desert-themed[/b]. Our development idea is to ensure each map reflects its respective biome style and characteristics.

[h3][b]GAME MODES[/b][/h3]
Yomaia also offers a diverse range of gameplay modes. [u]The main mode[/u], codenamed [b]Primal[/b], is a classic [b]survival mode[/b] that provides players with a semi-realistic or realistic experience. It captures the core gameplay of Yomaia, where players must survive in challenging environments. Additionally, we are introducing a [b]Sandbox mode[/b] for players who enjoy open-ended gameplay, allowing them to explore different dinosaur species and playstyles without the need for the progression found in the Survival mode. This mode, called [b]Survive The Hunt[/b], caters to sandbox enthusiasts. Furthermore, we have the traditional [b]Deathmatch or FFA[/b] (Free For All) mode, where all players can engage in combat, including [i]dinosaur versus dinosaur and human versus human[/i] battles. This mode is called [b]Rampage[/b]. These three modes are the primary ones that will likely be available during Early Access. However, we are also developing other concepts and playstyles. For example, "[i]Capture the Egg[/i]" is [i]a mode similar to Capture the Flag, incorporating elements of territorial control within the dinosaur theme[/i].
